summary: Defines an RTCP Source Description item and an RTCP Extended Report block that identify and describe a measurement period. Other XR blocks can refer to this period. It is a standards-track specification.

eli5.summary: When you time a race, you must say when the timing started and stopped. This memo gives real-time media reports a way to label that time window.

questions: how to identify measurement period in rtcp
what is rtcp measurement information block
what is the apsi sdes item
subtitle: A way to label which stretch of a call or stream an RTCP quality report is talking about.

tldr.problem: Several small RTCP XR metric blocks often describe the same stream and the same measurement period, and repeating the identifying details in each one would waste space.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines one Measurement Information XR block (block type 14) that carries sequence numbers and durations once, plus an APSI SDES item (type 10) for an application-specific identifier.
tldr.outcome: Other XR blocks can refer to one shared description of the measurement period instead of each carrying its own copy.

today: RFC 6776 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: What the Document Adds
sections.content:
RFC 6776 defines two small additions to the RTP Control Protocol (RTCP): one new Source Description (SDES) item and one new Extended Report (XR) block. Both carry parameters that identify and describe a measurement period, which one or more other RTCP XR blocks may refer to.

The XR block contains no measurement results. It only provides context for results reported in other block types, such as the sequence number of the first packet of the RTP session, the extended sequence numbers that bound the current measurement interval, the duration of the most recent interval and the duration of the interval used for cumulative measurements.
sections.eli5: Imagine many report cards for the same school term. Instead of writing the term dates on every card, you write them once on a cover sheet.

sections.title: Why One Shared Block
sections.content:
Commonly, several small metric blocks hold measurement data for the same stream and period. The RFC points out that the overhead would be large if each of them carried duplicate identification data. The Measurement Information block is meant to provide a single copy of what is needed to relate the measurements to the stream and period they refer to.

A block may be shared by a set of metric blocks, and an RTCP packet may hold several such sets. Blocks defined before this mechanism existed can sit in the same packet without being tied to a Measurement Information block. The XR block does not have to be in the same RTCP packet as the SDES item that carries the measurement identity.

The design follows the Performance Metrics Framework (RFC 6390) and builds on RTCP as defined in RFC 3550 and the XR structure from RFC 3611.
sections.eli5: Writing the same dates on every card wastes paper. One cover sheet that every card points to is neater.

sections.title: The APSI SDES Item
sections.content:
The Application-Specific Identifier (APSI) item rides in an RTCP SDES packet, whose PT field is set to SDES (202). The item starts with the type value APSI=10 and a length field, followed by a variable-length identifier. The length does not count the two-octet item header.

The identifier is useful in the context of a specific application. The RFC gives an MPEG-2 transport identifier as an example. It can be used to correlate data in XR blocks within an RTP session with data from a non-RTP session. Applications that are not configured to use the item MUST ignore it.
sections.eli5: It is a name tag you can stick on a stream so that a different system can recognise the same thing. Anyone who does not care about the tag just ignores it.

sections.title: The Measurement Information XR Block
sections.content:
The block starts with BT=14, an 8-bit reserved field and a 16-bit block length, which is always 7 (the length in 32-bit words minus one). Next comes the 32-bit SSRC of the stream source, as defined in RFC 3611. The reserved fields MUST be set to zero by senders and ignored by receivers.

The remaining fields are:

  • First sequence number (16 bits): the RTP sequence number of the first received packet of the session, used to work out how many packets contribute to cumulative measurements.
  • Extended first sequence number of interval (32 bits): the extended sequence number of the first received packet of the current measurement interval.
  • Extended last sequence number (32 bits): the extended sequence number of the last received packet that contributed to the measurement.
  • Measurement Duration (Interval) (32 bits): the length of the reporting interval, in units of 1/65536 seconds.
  • Measurement Duration (Cumulative) (64 bits): the length of the interval for cumulative reports, as a 64-bit NTP-format timestamp with the integer part in the first 32 bits and the fraction in the last 32.

An extended sequence number has the 16-bit sequence number from the RTP packet in the low half and the count of sequence number cycles in the high half. The receiver of the media stream can calculate the durations, for example from received RTP packets or with the RTCP method in RFC 3550.
sections.eli5: The block is a short form with boxes for the first and last packet numbers and for how long the timing lasted, once for the latest window and once for the whole call so far.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: The document adds the Measurement Identity item to the IANA RTP SDES item types registry as abbreviation APSI, name Application-Specific Identifier, value 10. It also assigns block type value 14 in the IANA RTCP XR Block Type Registry to the Measurement Information Block.
sections.eli5: The authors reserved two official numbers, like claiming two locker numbers so nobody else uses them.

sections.title: Security
sections.content: RTCP reports can contain sensitive information, including the nature and duration of a session between two or more endpoints. For that reason the security mechanisms for RTP described in Section 9 of RFC 3550 apply. The RFC defines no security machinery of its own.
sections.eli5: Reports can reveal who talked and for how long, so you should protect them the same way you protect the call itself.

fields.desc: First received RTP packet of the session.

fields.desc: First received packet of the current interval.

fields.name: Extended last sequence number
fields.desc: Last received packet that contributed to the measurement.

fields.name: Measurement Duration (Interval)
fields.desc: Interval length in units of 1/65536 seconds.

fields.desc: Integer part of the cumulative duration.

fields.name: Measurement Duration (Cumulative), fraction
fields.desc: Fractional part of the cumulative duration.
